newsitem.title: UK: Euroclear accepts Croatian kuna as settlement unit.
newsitem.headline: Euroclear accepts Croatian kuna as settlement unit.

text.p: Euroclear, a clearance and settlement system for international securities, said on Tuesday it had accepted the Croation kuna as a settlement currency.
The move, effective immediately, means the kuna will be accepted in money transfers and for internal settlement of transactions between participants, Euroclear said in a statement.

"Acceptance of the Croation kuna will benefit international investors wishing to participate in the first ever Eurobond offering by the Republic," Camille Lavirotte, an associate of Euroclear's market services division said in the statement.
In December Croatia issued 300 million kuna in maiden 12.5 percent, two-year Euro-domestic bonds maturing in 1998.
Euroclear, based in Brussels, added that Raiffeisenbank Austria in Zagreb serves as the Euroclear cash correspondent for the currency.
